record.paper_title: Open Problems on Open Algebraic Varieties (Montreal 1994 Problems)
record.original_question: If a homology sphere S occurs as the boundary of a strictly pseudoconvex domain in C^2, must S be diffeomorphic to the 3-sphere S^3?

evidence.quote: QUESTION. Let a homology sphere S be a boundary of a strictly pseudoconvex domain in C2. Is it true that then S is diﬀeomorphic to S3 ?

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let $S$ be a closed orientable 3-manifold that is an integral homology 3-sphere; that is, $H_*(S;\mathbb{Z}) \cong H_*(S^3;\mathbb{Z})$. Suppose there exists a bounded domain $\Omega \subset \mathbb{C}^2$ with smooth boundary $\partial\Omega$ such that $\partial\Omega$ is strictly pseudoconvex (i.e., $\Omega = \{\rho < 0\}$ for a smooth defining function $\rho$ with $d\rho \neq 0$ on $\partial\Omega$, and the Levi form of $\rho$ restricted to the complex tangent bundle of $\partial\Omega$ is positive definite), and suppose $\partial\Omega$ is diffeomorphic to $S$. Must $S$ be diffeomorphic to the standard 3-sphere $S^3$?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is closely related to a conjecture of Gompf stating that no nontrivial Brieskorn integer homology sphere admits a pseudoconvex embedding in $\mathbb{C}^2$ (with either orientation). The general question remains open, but partial results are known: Mark and Tosun (2018) verified Gompf's conjecture, in one orientation, for an infinite family of Brieskorn spheres. Thus the question is currently classified as partially solved / open.

status_evidence.title: Obstructing pseudoconvex embeddings and contractible Stein fillings for Brieskorn spheres
status_evidence.snippet: A conjecture due to Gompf asserts that no nontrivial Brieskorn homology sphere admits a pseudoconvex embedding in C^2, with either orientation.
status_evidence.claim: The general homology-sphere boundary question is captured by Gompf's still-open conjecture, with partial verification.

status_evidence.title: Obstructing pseudoconvex embeddings and contractible Stein fillings for Brieskorn spheres
status_evidence.snippet: Verified for a family of Brieskorn spheres, in one orientation.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress toward the conjecture has been made for infinite families.
